speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history suggestive of bone fragility. To better understand your condition, have you ever experienced fractures from minor trauma or falls?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly), virilization in the mother during pregnancy (hirsutism), delayed menarche, severe acne, and bone fragility in an adolescent female is highly characteristic of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. I will confirm this with a hormone panel and imaging.

REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, ACTH stimulation test, DHEA-S, and serum electrolytes.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_ultrasound.
